compatibility: Selected FreeDOS 3.1 physical-layout facts, implemented as an explicit extension in the existing Microsoft-format KEYB library. No claim that these are retail DOS 6.22 Baltic layouts.
id_policy: ET 454 and LT 221 follow reference numeric identifiers. LV has no numeric ID in the reference: this implementation assigns 0 to its sole/default LV entry. Other Baltic variants and non-775 keyboard pages are rejected.

mode_policy.basis: Existing KEYB hot-key behavior; no Russian Alt+Shift feature flags for these profiles.

modifiers.third_level: Right Alt or Ctrl+Alt; Shift selects the shifted third-level plane where the reference defines one.
modifiers.caps_lock: Swaps normal and Shift effects on C-marked keys only; does not change third-level planes.
modifiers.precedence: Third-level selection precedes plain Ctrl or Alt; use explicit Ctrl/Alt reference entries where present, otherwise preserve BIOS handling.
modifiers.fallback: Unassigned key/plane falls through common mapping and then the BIOS; explicit remapped scan codes are retained.
modifiers.hardware: Enhanced PC keyboard plus AT-84 and XT-83 where keys exist. Ctrl+Alt provides third-level access on keyboards without right Alt.
legacy_exclusions: Physical scan 86 (extra ISO key) and separate right Alt/Ctrl are unavailable on AT-84/XT-83.
Unavailable physical keys are not injected or counted as tested; national letters must still be reachable through the supported keys.

composition.table: Use every selected CP775 dead-key pair and literal from the retained reference. Lithuanian LST 1582 has no CP775 dead keys.
composition.space: Dead key plus space emits its literal once.
composition.unmatched: Emit the pending literal followed by the new character, then clear pending state.
composition.controls: Qualify pending-state cleanup, cancellation/reload, repeated dead keys and ordinary control/navigation input in the guest.
composition.scan_scope: Explicit reference scan remaps are frozen. Composition/fallback scan behavior must be compared with the existing KEYB interpreter before finalizing physical BIOS expectations.

remaining: Implement Baltic data/logic in KEYBRD2.SYS while preserving RU.
Qualify full modifier precedence and pending-composition control behavior against actual guest output.
Run both BIOS/DOS byte tests and supported legacy-hardware matrices with all BALTIC.md integration/release gates.
